###### Rosh Hashanah 25b:13
[Rosh Hashanah 25b:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Rosh%20Hashanah/r/25b:13)

וְאֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי? אָמַר קְרָא: ״כִּי חֹק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא מִשְׁפָּט לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב״, אֵימַת הָוֵי ״חֹק״ — בִּגְמַר דִּין, וְקָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא ״מִשְׁפָּט״, מָה מִשְׁפָּט בַּיּוֹם — אַף הָכָא נָמֵי בַּיּוֹם.

**William Davidson Edition - English:**
The Gemara raises another difficulty: **Why not say** that, **indeed,** the sanctification of the month should be treated like monetary cases? The Gemara answers: **The verse states** with regard to Rosh HaShana: **“For this is a statute for Israel, a judgment [*mishpat*] of the God of Jacob”** (Psalms 81:5). **When does** the sanctification of the month **become a statute? At the end of the judicial process, and the Merciful One calls it a judgment** as well, thereby teaching that **just as** the primary time of **a judgment is during the day, here too,** with regard to the sanctification of the New Moon, the process must take place **during the day,** and not at night.

# Beit Yaakov on Torah: Toldos · Ois 15 — Balancing Yitzchak Through Avraham and Yaakov · תּוֹלְדוֹת, אוֹת ט״ו
Ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Toldot 15 · בית יעקב על התורה, תּוֹלְדוֹת, אוֹת ט״ו

**Balancing Yitzchak Through Avraham and Yaakov**
**Translation note: the rare word מגנוניא is retained as genunya; its precise reading and meaning remain uncertain.**
**Holy Restraint and Life in This World**
**Bashfulness and the World to Come**
**Avraham and Yitzchak Clarify One Another**
[Beit Yaakov on Torah, Toldot 15:1]
אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק. — Avraham fathered Yitzchak.
אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ מגנוניא שֶׁלִּי הוּא וְכוּלֵי. — The Midrash states: ‘He is of My genunya,’ and so forth.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ הַמִּדְרָשׁ, — The Midrash means
שֶׁכָּל הַהַנְהָגוֹת שֶׁמִּסְתָּעֲפִים וְהוֹלְכִים מִיִּצְחָק אָבִינוּ, — that all the modes of conduct that branch out from Yitzchak our father
מִיָּד תּוֹפֵס אוֹתָם אַבְרָהָם מִצַּד אֶחָד וְיַעֲקֹב מִצַּד הַשֵּׁנִי. — are immediately held in check by Avraham on one side and Yaakov on the other.
וְהַיְינוּ כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (תּוֹלְדוֹת קמב.) — This accords with the holy Zohar, Toldos 142a,
שֶׁיִּצְחָק אָבִינוּ הוּא וְלַחֹשֶׁךְ קָרָא לָיְלָה, — that Yitzchak our father corresponds to ‘and the darkness He called night.’
שֶׁרָצָה לְהַטְמִין כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת עַל לֶעָתִיד, — He wished to store away all good things for the future,
וּבָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה יוּצְרַךְ צִמְצוּמִים הַרְבֵּה, — while in this world much restraint would be required.
וְלָכֵן אֵינָם יְכוֹלִים הַבְּרוּאִים לְקַבֵּל זֶה הָאוֹר, — Created beings therefore cannot receive this light.
וְלָכֵן אַבְרָהָם תּוֹפֵס אוֹתוֹ מִצַּד אֶחָד וְיַעֲקֹב מִצַּד אֶחָד, — Avraham therefore holds him on one side and Yaakov on the other,
שֶׁהֵם מַרְאִים שֶׁגַּם עוֹלָם הַזֶּה בָּרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, — showing that Hashem, blessed be He, also created this world.
וְאִם לֹא יַזִּיק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא מוּתָּר לֵיהָנוֹת מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה. — If it does not harm one's portion in the World to Come, one may enjoy this world.
וְלָכֵן כְּתִיב אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק, — The verse therefore says, ‘Avraham fathered Yitzchak,’
שֶׁיֹּאחַז מְעַט בְּמִדַּת אַבְרָהָם. — so that Yitzchak should hold somewhat to Avraham's attribute.
וְגַם אַבְרָהָם הוּבְרַר בָּזֶה, — Avraham, too, was clarified through this,
כִּי מַה שֶּׁנָּטַע בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מִדַּת בַּיְשָׁנִים הוּא מִיִּצְחָק, — for the quality of bashfulness planted in Israel comes from Yitzchak.
וְלָזֶה אוּמּוֹת אֵין לָהֶם בּוּשָׁה, — For this reason the nations lack this sense of shame,
כִּי מִי שֶׁמִּתְבַּיֵּישׁ יֵשׁ לוֹ חַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, — for one who feels shame has life in the World to Come.
כִּי מִדַּת יִצְחָק הוּא לְהַטְמִין הַתַּקִּיפוּת עַל הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, — Yitzchak's attribute is to reserve strength for the World to Come,
כִּי אַבְרָהָם הָיָה עוֹסֵק כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו — whereas Avraham labored throughout his life
שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ כָּל הַבְּרוּאִים מְלוּכַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. — so that all created beings would recognize the sovereignty of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ הָיָה אוֹמֵר — Yitzchak our father would say:
כָּל תַּלְמִיד שֶׁאֵין תּוֹכוֹ כְּבָרוֹ אַל יִכָּנֵס לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, — ‘Any student whose inner character does not match his outward appearance should not enter the house of study.’
וְלָכֵן צָר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ קְלַסְתֵּר פָּנָיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק דּוֹמֶה לְאַבְרָהָם, — Hashem, blessed be He, therefore formed Yitzchak's features to resemble Avraham's,
שֶׁיִּצְחָק בֵּירֵר כָּל מַעֲשֵׂי אַבְרָהָם שֶׁהֵם רְצוּיִים וְטוֹבִים, — for Yitzchak clarified that all Avraham's deeds were desirable and good.
וְאַבְרָהָם בֵּירֵר בְּהוֹלִידוֹ אֶת יִצְחָק — By fathering Yitzchak, Avraham established
שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁהִכְנִיס לַקְּדוּשָּׁה הָיָה מְבוֹרָר: — that everything he had brought into holiness had been clarified.
